#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and wait for it — NEVER kill it (gh-1903).
# Shared by every dispatching daily-publish leg.
#
# gh-1903 invariant: a child run QUEUED behind siblings on the single
# self-hosted runner (fa-m5-1) is NORMAL OPERATION, not a failure mode.
# The 2026-10-26 incident (daily run 40274465122, issue #1735) cancelled
# TWO healthy queued testflight children (~31m "queue stall" each) and
# failed a fully-built v1.0.648 release solely by killing its place in
# line. What remains here:
#   * dispatch + exact run correlation, unchanged (#343 below);
#   * a read-only wait: child state + elapsed logged every poll, sibling
#     in-progress runs logged on a diagnostic interval while the child has
#     not started — NO stall timer, NO wedge cancel, NO re-dispatch;
#   * bounds: the child's own per-job server-side timeouts (#344) and the
#     leg's timeout-minutes — nothing else;
#   * exactly ONE cancel path: when the LEG itself is terminated (leg
#     timeout, manual cancel → this script gets TERM/INT), cancel only
#     THIS leg's own NEVER-STARTED child (by the already-correlated run
#     id) so an orphaned queued run cannot publish unattended when the
#     pool revives, then fail with a diagnostic naming the child run, its
#     last observed state, and the observed pool activity. A child that
#     ever started, or already completed, is never touched.
#
# The watchdog it replaces (kept for history): #344 budgeted the watch
# (~2x historical duration) and cancelled + re-dispatched a wedged run
# once; gh-172 added a queue-stall window (no in_progress job for
# max(600, budget/8)s) for the pool-held zombie (run 39374894901). Both
# heuristics false-positive on healthy queues by construction — 31m does
# not cover the cli sibling chain's 335m worst-case on the same runner —
# and each cancel loses the queue position and restarts the clock, a
# starvation loop. Zombie handling is now: CANNOT OBSERVE ⇒ CANNOT JUDGE.
# The repo-wide `gh run list --status in_progress` probe is read-only; if
# it shows runs, the queue is presumed healthy; if it shows none while the
# child never started, a ::warning:: names the gh-172 zombie signature and
# the leg timeout surfaces the full diagnostic. Only a repo-wide EMPTY
# in_progress list while the child never started positively establishes
# pool idleness — and even then the script does not cancel (gh-1903).
#
# #343 — correlation (unchanged): the TestFlight and Play legs dispatch
# the SAME workflow (build-mobile.yml) as concurrent `needs: plan`
# siblings; identifying "our" run by event + a createdAt window only let
# the Play leg latch the TestFlight run. Correlation here:
#   * exact displayTitle match (--title) — the child workflow's run-name
#     embeds its inputs, so the sibling's differently-shaped run can never
#     be adopted (`gh run list` cannot filter by inputs; displayTitle is
#     the only distinguisher in the list API);
#   * the NEWEST matching run ([-1]) — never [0];
#   * a tight 30s createdAt window (clock-skew headroom; a run from
#     minutes ago is out of scope).
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the wait), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_DIAG_SECONDS (300 — sibling-liveness probe interval while the child
# has not started; 0 = every poll).
set -euo pipefail

# ─ gh-1903 orphan backstop (re-invocation mode) ────────────────────────────
# The watcher installs a detached BACKSTOP once its child run is correlated.
# Rationale (bash 5.3 / ubuntu-26.04, 2026-10-29 CI reds on main b54f324c
# and PR #1958 6a49b3ec): run_pending_traps can fire while the shell's
# parser holds a half-read construct (input.c's read loop and eval.c's
# parse_command both call it), and the trap ACTION STRING is then parsed in
# that poisoned state — bash prints `trap: line 2: unexpected EOF while
# looking for matching ')'` and exits 2 WITHOUT running orphan_cleanup. The
# trap handler parse is therefore not a containment guarantee, so the
# backstop owns the same decision independently: if the watcher dies without
# the handler having marked "$2/handler-ran" (poisoned parse, SIGKILL after
# a wedged signal handoff, any death mode), cancel the never-started child
# exactly like the handler would — gh-1903 contract verbatim: never-started
# children only, exactly one cancel (the handler marks itself BEFORE its own
# gh call, so backstop and handler can never double-cancel).
if [ "${1:-}" = "--dw-orphan-backstop" ]; then
  backstop_parent="$2"
  backstop_state="$3"
  backstop_run_id="$4"
  backstop_repo="$5"
  backstop_workflow="$6"
  while kill -0 "$backstop_parent" 2>/dev/null; do
    # The state dir is the watcher's side of the contract: it is removed on
    # every deliberate stop (stop_orphan_backstop). If it is gone while the
    # PID still answers (recycled PID), stop anyway — never a leaked
    # process on the shared pool (#1001 hygiene).
    [ -e "$backstop_state" ] || exit 0
    sleep "${DW_BACKSTOP_POLL_SECONDS:-1}"
  done
  if [ -e "$backstop_state/handler-ran" ]; then
    rm -rf "$backstop_state" 2>/dev/null || true
    exit 0
  fi
  if [ -e "$backstop_state/child-started" ]; then
    rm -rf "$backstop_state" 2>/dev/null || true
    exit 0
  fi
  backstop_status="$(gh run view "$backstop_run_id" --repo "$backstop_repo" \
    --json status --jq .status 2>/dev/null)" || backstop_status=""
  if [ "$backstop_status" = "completed" ]; then
    rm -rf "$backstop_state" 2>/dev/null || true
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "::error::dispatch_and_watch: watcher died without running the orphan-cleanup handler (trap-action parse loss?) — backstop cancelling never-started child $backstop_workflow run $backstop_run_id (gh-1903 containment)" >&2
  gh run cancel "$backstop_run_id" --repo "$backstop_repo" \
    || echo "::warning::backstop orphan cancel of run $backstop_run_id failed (already gone?)" >&2
  rm -rf "$backstop_state" 2>/dev/null || true
  exit 0
fi

workflow=""
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
ref="main"
title=""
out_run_id=""
inputs=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) repo="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref) ref="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --title) title="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out-run-id) out_run_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -f) inputs+=( -f "$2" ); shift 2 ;;
    -*) echo "dispatch_and_watch: unknown flag: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *)
      if [ -n "$workflow" ]; then
        echo "dispatch_and_watch: unexpected extra arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
      fi
      workflow="$1"; shift
      ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$workflow" ] || [ -z "$repo" ]; then
  echo "usage: dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO [--ref main] [--title T] [--out-run-id FILE] [-f k=v]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
diag="${DW_DIAG_SECONDS:-300}"

# jq selector: optional exact displayTitle match (#343).
title_select=""
if [ -n "$title" ]; then
  title_select=" | select(.displayTitle == \"${title}\")"
fi

dispatch() {
  gh workflow run "$workflow" --repo "$repo" --ref "$ref" ${inputs[@]+"${inputs[@]}"}
}

# The id of OUR run: workflow_dispatch runs created at/after the floor,
# matching --title when given, NEWEST of the matches (#343).
find_run_id() {
  local floor="$1"
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow "$workflow" --event workflow_dispatch \
    --limit 20 --json databaseId,createdAt,displayTitle \
    --jq "[.[] | select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) >= $floor)${title_select}] | sort_by(.createdAt) | .[-1].databaseId // 0" \
    2>/dev/null || echo 0
}

wait_for_run() {
  local floor="$1" id=0 i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt "$appear_attempts" ]; do
    id=$(find_run_id "$floor")
    if [ "$id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "$id"; return 0; fi
    sleep "$appear_poll"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  return 1
}

# ── gh-1903 single cancel path: the orphan-cleanup trap ────────────────────
# Leg timeout / manual cancel make the runner TERM (then KILL) this
# script. On TERM/INT: if OUR child was never started and is not completed,
# cancel exactly that run (gh-172 containment — an orphaned queued run
# must not publish unattended when the pool revives) and fail naming the
# child, its last observed state, and the observed pool activity. A child
# that ever started — even if it is between jobs right now — is left
# alone: its own per-job server-side timeouts (#344) bound it.
#
# The handler marks "$dw_state/handler-ran" BEFORE its first gh call so the
# detached backstop (spawned at the correlation site below) can tell a
# handled death from a lost handler and never double-cancel. DW_TRAP_PARSE_
# DEATH=1 (test shim) installs a deliberately unparseable trap action,
# reproducing the bash-5.3 poisoned-parse death (exit 2, handler never runs)
# that lost the orphan-cancel on CI reds main b54f324c / PR #1958 6a49b3ec.
run_id=0
child_started=0
watch_started=0
last_state="(never polled)"
pool_note="no pool observation yet"
dw_state=""

orphan_cleanup() {
  local sig="$1" ec=143 now
  [ "$sig" = "INT" ] && ec=130
  if [ -n "$dw_state" ]; then
    : > "$dw_state/handler-ran" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  now=$(date +%s)
  if [ "$run_id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null \
      && [ "$child_started" -eq 0 ] \
      && [ "${last_state%%/*}" != "completed" ]; then
    echo "::error::leg terminated by $sig after $((now - watch_started))s — child $workflow run $run_id NEVER STARTED (last observed: $last_state; $pool_note); cancelling this orphaned child only (gh-1903 orphan-cancel) — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
    gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
      || echo "::warning::orphan cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)" >&2
  else
    echo "::error::leg terminated by $sig after $((now - watch_started))s — child $workflow run $run_id (started: $([ "$child_started" -eq 1 ] && echo yes || echo no); last observed: $last_state; $pool_note); nothing to cancel (gh-1903: never-started children only)" >&2
  fi
  exit "$ec"
}
if [ "${DW_TRAP_PARSE_DEATH:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  # Test shim: the action string the bash-5.3 poisoned parser dies on
  # (unbalanced `(` — parser_error → exit 2, orphan_cleanup never runs).
  trap 'orphan_cleanup TERM ( ' TERM
  trap 'orphan_cleanup INT ( ' INT
else
  trap 'orphan_cleanup TERM' TERM
  trap 'orphan_cleanup INT' INT
fi

dispatch
epoch=$(date +%s)
if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
  echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id — read-only wait, no stall timer, no re-dispatch (gh-1903)"
if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

# ─ gh-1903 orphan backstop: the cancel must not depend on the trap parse ───
# Spawned AFTER correlation (a run id exists to cancel) and detached via
# setsid where available, so a leg-timeout tree-kill cannot take it down
# with the watcher. Stopped explicitly on every NORMAL exit; on a handler
# exit it self-terminates after seeing the handler-ran marker.
dw_backstop_pid=""
dw_state="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dw-orphan-XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" || dw_state=""
stop_orphan_backstop() {
  if [ -n "$dw_backstop_pid" ]; then
    kill "$dw_backstop_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$dw_backstop_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    dw_backstop_pid=""
  fi
  if [ -n "$dw_state" ]; then
    rm -rf "$dw_state" 2>/dev/null || true
    dw_state=""
  fi
}
if [ -n "$dw_state" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$dw_state/run-id"
  if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    setsid bash "$0" --dw-orphan-backstop "$$" "$dw_state" "$run_id" "$repo" "$workflow" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
  else
    bash "$0" --dw-orphan-backstop "$$" "$dw_state" "$run_id" "$repo" "$workflow" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
  fi
  dw_backstop_pid=$!
fi

watch_started=$(date +%s)
last_diag=0
while :; do

  # running-job count arrive atomically — no race where two calls
  # straddle a completion. A failed poll cannot observe, so it cannot
  # judge (gh-172): it is logged and the wait simply continues — the
  # bounds are the child's per-job server-side timeouts (#344) and the
  # leg timeout, and there is no heuristic left to poison.
  observed="$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
    --jq '"\(.status)/" + (.conclusion // "-") + " " + ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring)' 2>/dev/null)" || observed=""
  if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "${observed%% *}" = "$observed" ]; then
    status="error/-"
    running=""
    last_state="$status"
    echo "poll failed (gh/API unreachable) after $(( $(date +%s) - watch_started ))s — cannot observe, cannot judge (gh-172); the wait continues"
  else
    status="${observed%% *}"
    running="${observed##* }"
    last_state="$status"

      child_started=1
      # The backstop reads the flag from disk (it outlives this shell).
      if [ -n "$dw_state" ]; then
        printf '1\n' > "$dw_state/child-started" 2>/dev/null || true
      fi
    fi
    echo "child $run_id: $status running_jobs=${running:-unknown} elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - watch_started ))s (started: $([ "$child_started" -eq 1 ] && echo yes || echo 'not yet — queued is healthy, gh-1903'))"
  fi
  if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
  now=$(date +%s)

  # probe repo-wide liveness on the diagnostic interval. This NEVER
  # cancels — it only distinguishes "queued behind siblings" (healthy)

  # zombie signature, surfaced in full at the leg timeout above).
  if [ "$child_started" -eq 0 ] && [ $((now - last_diag)) -ge "$diag" ]; then
    last_diag="$now"
    if sibs="$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --status in_progress --limit 20 \
        --json databaseId,displayTitle \
        --jq '[.[] | select(.databaseId != '"$run_id"')] | length as $n | "\($n) in_progress run(s): " + ([.[] | "\(.databaseId) \(.displayTitle)"] | join("; "))' 2>/dev/null)"; then
      if [ "${sibs%% *}" = "0" ]; then

        echo "::warning::$pool_note — NO cancel (gh-1903); if this is a real zombie the leg timeout surfaces the full diagnostic"
      else

        echo "sibling activity — $sibs — the queued child is waiting behind these; healthy, no cancel, no stall timer (gh-1903)"
      fi

      pool_note="pool liveness probe FAILED (gh/API unreachable) — pool idleness can be neither established nor excluded"

    fi

# backstop here could only misread the state dir and double-act.
stop_orphan_backstop

# gate; warnings/infos pass, matching the static analyze stage.
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub get && dart analyze)
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings)

  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # gh-1778: 20 min — sized for the degraded-cache worst case, not just
    # the warm wall. Warm shards take ~460-525 s (run 39703080550) but the
    # v1.0.621 release run stalled ~133 s on EACH cache step (degraded
    # GitHub cache service, keys that existed) and needed ~14 min cold —
    # cancelled at the 12-min wall with 2535/2761 tests green, reding the
    # whole release. 20 clears that worst case and sits in the sibling
    # test-leg band (flutter-tests 20, integration-mock 25, pty 40); a
    # genuinely hung shard is still killed loudly.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      # gh-1778: caches are best-effort — a restore that hangs (degraded
      # cache service stalled both steps ~133 s on the v1.0.621 release
      # run) or fails only means slower setup. Step-level 2-min cap bounds
      # the stall; continue-on-error keeps a dead cache from reding the
      # shard (unlike the gh-1724 evidence uploads, which stay loud).
      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-
        timeout-minutes: 2
        continue-on-error: true

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
        timeout-minutes: 2
        continue-on-error: true

      # gh-2072 (review thread 5): the prewarm is scope-gated EXACTLY like
      # the pub get above it — on an out-of-scope PR checkout/setup-dart/
      # pub get are all skipped (the fastpass keeps the leg green in
      # seconds) and an unconditional prewarm would red the required
      # contexts: the composite action file isn't even on disk without
      # checkout, and the script hard-fails without the pub get's package
      # config.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p build/test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:build/test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            build/test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            build/test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

**Bug**: The v1.0.739 tag CI run ([44024131629](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/44024131629)) failed `Core tests (shard 3/4)` — 3703 passed / **1 failed** / 5 skipped — and `Quality gate` red only as the aggregate of that shard.

**Root cause**: A one-shot wedged signal handoff in the gh-1903 INT orphan-cancel test (`test/dispatch_watch_test.dart`, group `gh-1903 — orphan-cancel fires only when the LEG dies` → `INT (manual workflow cancel) with a never-started child → the same single orphan-cancel`). The test spawns `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` as a live bash process, sends SIGINT after two poll anchors and expects the orphan-cleanup trap to cancel the never-started child and exit 130. In the red run the watcher's diagnostics prove the trap **never ran**: the poll loop continued at its 1s cadence from `elapsed=0s` through `elapsed=31s` with no `::error::leg terminated` line, no `run cancel 77` in the stub-gh log and no `cancelled-77` marker — the signal was silently lost/blocked rather than deferred (a deferred trap fires after at most one 1s poll sleep). `DwLive.finish()` then hit its 30s budget, SIGKILLed the watcher and threw `Bad state: process did not exit after signal` (test/dispatch_watch_test.dart:405), while the package:test 30s test timeout fired in parallel. This is the same wedged-signal-handoff flake family the test file itself documents from prior load-dependent reds (hostile-env red on b93d825b — the identical `process did not exit after signal` in this identical INT test; #1924 validation red; gh-1986 head ab81cbfa run 41035084398; validation red on 6f855aa34f run 41041694087).

**Impact**: CI-only. One test in one shard of one run; the same test-family's TERM cases passed seconds before/after in the same shard (05:32:03 TERM never-started ✓, 05:32:36 parse-death TERM ✓), so only the INT delivery wedged in that invocation. No product behavior is affected: `dispatch_and_watch.sh` still carries the orphan-cleanup trap AND the detached `--dw-orphan-backstop` that cancels a never-started child even when the trap is lost.

**Not a product defect — evidence**:
- Same commit `c08bbe2` passed the identical job on the same runners 4× today: runs 44003156628 (02:27), 44013020032 (03:50), 44017239294 (04:26), 44019813250 (04:49) — all four green including `Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Quality gate` (verified via job listings, real executions not scope skips).
- Locally at this commit: full `dart test test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — 28/28 green including the failing INT test; the INT test alone 5/5 green under 4-core CPU saturation (`while :; do :; done` ×4).
- Signal-disposition probes (dart 3.14.0, `/proc/self/status` masks main thread vs thread-pool isolate, with and without an active `sigint.watch()`): SIGINT is never SIG_IGN and never blocked in spawned bash children — no deterministic wedge exists in the code path.
- `git log origin/main..HEAD` = 0 commits — the failing tag points at exactly the code that was green 4× the same day; no diff exists to regress.

**Fix approach**: None required — the red is content-independent (flake), so no code change and no PR. Per repo policy the tag ref goes green on the next push/retrigger; the ci-red ticket closes when the ref is green ("Closes manually when the ref goes green", per the ticket body). Quarantine (`scripts/test_quarantine.json`) is out of scope: it covers integration-gate legs only, and flake-watch owns automated flake filing for unit suites.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first occurrence of this red on v1.0.739.

## Summary

**gh-2231 `[ci-red] v1.0.739 failed` — resolved as a CI flake, not a product defect (already-fixed classification, no code change, no PR).**

**What failed:** v1.0.739 tag run ([44024131629](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/44024131629)): `Core tests (shard 3/4)` — 3703 passed / **1 failed** — and `Quality gate` (aggregate collapse). The one failure: `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` → *gh-1903 INT orphan-cancel test*: the spawned `dispatch_and_watch.sh` watcher never acted on SIGINT — its poll loop ran smoothly at 1s cadence from `elapsed=0s` to `elapsed=31s` (proving bash was alive and the trap was never even deferred — no trap diagnostic, no `run cancel`, no exit), until `DwLive.finish()` SIGKILLed it at its 30s budget.

**Why flake, not regression:**
- The tag points at `c08bbe2`, which passed the **identical** job 4× the same day (runs 44003156628, 44013020032, 44017239294, 44019813250 — all four `Core tests` shards + `Quality gate` green, real executions not scope-skips).
- Locally: the failing test passes (full file 28/28; INT test 5/5 under 4-core CPU saturation); signal-disposition probes show no deterministic SIGINT ignore/block path on dart 3.14.0.
- It is the same documented wedged-signal-handoff family the test file itself lists from prior reds (b93d825b, #1924, gh-1986 run 41035084398, 6f855aa34f run 41041694087). TERM signal tests passed seconds before/after in the same shard.
- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` is correct: the orphan-cleanup trap is backstopped by the detached `--dw-orphan-backstop`, so the gh-1903 never-started-cancel contract holds even when a trap handoff is lost.

**Deliverables:** `outputs/rca.md` (full RCA with evidence), `outputs/already_fixed.json` (gh-2229 precedent format), `outputs/response.md` (ticket comment), `outputs/gh-2231/scope_estimate.json` (outcome: completed). Ticket closes when the ref goes green on the next push/retrigger, per the ticket body.

Final answer: the v1.0.739 CI red is a one-shot SIGINT-handoff flake in `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` (gh-1903 INT orphan-cancel) — classified already-fixed/flake with full RCA evidence; no product code change is warranted, and the artifacts (`outputs/rca.md`, `outputs/already_fixed.json`, `outputs/response.md`, `outputs/gh-2231/scope_estimate.json`) are in place for the pipeline.
